rationale: The text reports a commentator's bullish view on McDonald's stock, which is an investor/analyst sentiment item about the stock.

The headline event is Citigroup selling its German retail business to Credit Mutuel, a divestiture that fits mergers_acquisitions. The capital-raising motive also touches capital_shareholder_returns, but the deal itself is the story.

The story is about Meta and Snap shares rising on a commissioner's call to ban TikTok, a stock price move driven by sentiment about a rival. The regulatory comment concerns TikTok, not Meta, so the headline event is the share move.

The text previews upcoming quarterly results and per-share earnings estimates for Bank of America and peers, which is about results and guidance. The year-to-date stock gains are secondary context, so earnings_performance is the headline event.

The text reports Amazon's Prime Day sales event being on track to be its biggest sales day, a promotional/retail event rather than a product launch or financial results. It is closest to product_innovation as a commercial offering/event, though earnings_performance is defensible since it concerns sales figures.
The text centers on quarterly results that beat estimates, with revenue figures and cloud growth; the 4% share move is a reaction to those results, so earnings_performance is the headline event.
The text centers on a stock price move and an analyst's initiation of coverage with an outperform rating, which is market analyst sentiment.

The text centers on quarterly results that missed estimates and full-year guidance that also missed forecasts, which is earnings performance; the after-hours share move is a reaction to those results and does not change the headline event.

The headline event is Seth Klarman's Baupost building a $195 million stake in Dollar General, a famous investor buying the stock, which is investor_activity. The mention of the stock's decline is secondary context, not the story.
The text is about GE's plan to spin off its energy businesses as GE Vernova, a corporate break-up/divestiture that fits mergers_acquisitions.

The headline event is a price cut on AT&T's shared data plans, which rule 7 classifies as 'other' even though the share price moved. The stock decline is a reaction to the pricing action, not an analyst rating or investor stake change.

The headline event is a fund (Central Bank & Trust) cutting its stake in Humana per an SEC filing, which is investor activity. The share price move is a consequence of that stake sale, so market_analyst_sentiment is only weakly defensible.
The text is just a ticker list (NFLX, TSLA) with no substantive news about Netflix, so it fits no specific dimension and falls under other.
The text reports an analyst raising a price target and expressing a positive view on Amazon, which is squarely analyst sentiment.

The text centers on Qualcomm's resistance to a takeover deal and its rejection of record-breaking price tags, which is a deal/takeover story. The 5% share drop is a market reaction to that deal news, so market_analyst_sentiment is a defensible secondary label.

The text centers on Musk's SEC fraud settlement and his mocking of the regulator, a regulatory/legal action against the company's CEO. It could also be framed as leadership/governance given the CEO's conduct, but the SEC settlement is the headline event.
The text is an investor's bullish view on the 'Super Six' stocks including Amazon, discussing entry points and chart levels, which is a stock-price/analyst-sentiment story.
The text is about Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo raising his price target on Bank of America and calling for upside, which is analyst sentiment.
The Nucor mention is a stock price move (gaining around 7%), which is market sentiment; the earnings warning belongs to Semtech, not Nucor.
The text centers on Cowen's analyst picks and its $155 price target on Dollar Tree ahead of earnings, which is analyst sentiment. The upcoming earnings report is only the context for the call.

The text centers on Cummins' first-quarter profit more than doubling on strong international sales and a recovering North American truck market, which is a results story. The 8% share pop is a reaction to those results, so earnings_performance is the headline event.
The text centers on PepsiCo's attempt to buy its two largest bottlers and the potential pressure on Coca-Cola to make a similar move with its bottler, which is a deal/takeover story.
The text is a fragmentary mention of IBM within a list of dividend stocks and an index-impact comment, with no clear single news event about IBM itself.

The headline event is Morgan Stanley reiterating TransDigm as its top pick and staying bullish, which is analyst sentiment. The lowered earnings outlook is background context that prompted the analyst view.

The text reflects on earnings news from Apple and Google and how companies missing Wall Street estimates get punished, making results and guidance the headline event. The discussion of analyst estimates and investor reactions is secondary to the earnings theme.

The text centers on a strategist's bullish technical view and price target ($115) for Dollar General ahead of its earnings, which is analyst/investor sentiment about the stock. Earnings is only the upcoming catalyst, not the reported figures themselves.
The text is a collection of analyst actions, including Bank of America reiterating Nvidia as a buy and calling it a top idea, which is analyst sentiment on the stock.
The Centene item is a Wells Fargo analyst downgrade to equal weight with a price target cut, which is squarely an analyst rating/price target story.
The text centers on the break-up of Hewlett-Packard into HP Inc and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, a corporate separation/divestiture, which fits mergers_acquisitions.
The text is a commentator's bullish view that Cummins will benefit from a new truck cycle, which is an investor's bullish opinion on the stock.

The text is a roundup of traders' final trades and positions, including GOOGL, which is an investor/analyst-style bullish or bearish view on the stock. It fits market_analyst_sentiment as commentary on stock positioning rather than company news.
The text reports a proposed merger between Citigroup and Bank of America, which is a deal/takeover story.

The text describes a solar power agreement (a deal) signed by Microsoft in India, which is a business development/partnership arrangement rather than a product or earnings event. No other label fits well, though 'other' is a weak fallback.
The text is commentary from LPL Financial expressing a bullish view on Uber's stock, which is analyst/investor sentiment about the stock rather than a company event.

The text centers on the upcoming tech earnings reports from Apple and Amazon and how earnings could affect the stocks, which is an earnings event. The investor commentary on long-term prospects and past gains is secondary sentiment around that earnings story.

The text reports Berkshire Hathaway, a famous investor, selling nearly half of its Apple stake, which is a fund/investor buying or selling the stock. The mention of Apple's selling streak is a stock price move, but the headline event is the investor's stake sale.
The text reports quarterly profit and revenue figures versus consensus, which is a results story.
The headline event is Schwab's talks to acquire TD Ameritrade, a takeover story. The mention of Bettinger running the combined company is a secondary detail of the deal.

The headline event is Hormel's quarterly results, which matched EPS estimates but missed on revenue, making earnings_performance the primary dimension. The CytoSport sale to PepsiCo is a secondary deal element mentioned separately.

The text is a TV host's bullish stock-picking view on Abbott Labs, citing its dividend yield and management, which is an investor's sentiment on the stock. The dividend yield mention is secondary context rather than a company dividend action.

The text centers on production cuts at six Ford plants, which is a workforce/manufacturing reduction event, making labor_human_capital the closest fit. It is not about results, deals, or products, so 'other' is the only alternative.

The text centers on analysts expecting Target to fight to keep its market-leading position against Wal-Mart, which is analyst sentiment about competitive standing. No results, deals, or corporate actions are named, so 'other' is a weak fallback.

The text is about restarting production and plant closures affecting the workforce, with safety measures for returning workers, which fits workforce and labour relations. It is not about results, deals, or product launches.

The headline event is Roku's exclusive advertising partnership with Amazon, a strategic alliance, so partnerships_business_dev fits best. The stock move is a reaction to the deal, making market_analyst_sentiment a weaker second option.

The text reports that a well-known investor, Pete Najarian, bought PayPal stock, which is a fund or famous investor buying the stock and fits investor_activity. A defensible alternative is market_analyst_sentiment, since Najarian is a market commentator expressing a bullish view, but the headline event is the purchase itself.

The text centers on multiple price target cuts from analysts on CrowdStrike despite beating numbers, making analyst sentiment the headline event. The earnings beat is mentioned but the story is the analyst reactions and target cuts.

The text centers on the regulatory grounding of the 737 Max by authorities after fatal crashes and Boeing's abandoned projection that regulators would lift it, which is a regulatory action on the company. The fatal crashes and grounding also damage Boeing's public standing, making reputational_harm defensible.
The text centers on Cramer recommending BHP acquire Freeport-McMoRan, a takeover/deal scenario, which is mergers_acquisitions. The analyst's bullish view is secondary commentary on that deal idea.

The text previews upcoming earnings reports for Citigroup and peers and discusses expected share moves around those results, making results the headline event. The stock-price and options-market commentary is secondary context to the earnings preview.
The text is a stock-picking recommendation favoring Gilead or Bristol-Myers Squibb, which is an investor/analyst bullish view on the stock.

The text is about UPS halting heavy-item pickups ahead of a union contract vote and to avoid disruptions from a potential work stoppage, which is a workforce and labour relations matter. The service change tied to labour risk could also be framed as a service failure affecting public standing.

The headline event is Wells Fargo reiterating its equal-weight rating on Tesla, an analyst call, which fits market_analyst_sentiment. The underlying subject is a reported Tesla bid for Sigma Lithium, a deal story, but the analyst's reaction does not change the headline event.
The text describes Time Warner Cable's deal with Charter after Comcast's bid collapsed, which is a takeover/merger event.

The text describes a trader's bullish options trade and view on Bank of America, which is an investor/trader sentiment view on the stock rather than company news. It fits market_analyst_sentiment as a bullish view on the shares.
The text centers on Twitter's talks with Apple to bring the Twitter app to Apple TV, a strategic distribution/alliance discussion, making partnerships_business_dev the headline event.

The headline event is Oppenheimer initiating an outperform rating with a $90 price target, which is analyst sentiment. The Amazon-Whole Foods acquisition is discussed as context, making mergers_acquisitions a defensible secondary label.

The text is about an executive hire (Doug Field) and his reporting line to the CEO, which is a leadership/governance event. The connected-vehicle and software context is secondary background to the appointment.

The text centers on Teradyne's quarterly results and outlook beating analyst estimates, with the 19% share surge as a reaction to the earnings report. Per rule 2, results with guidance and a share move are earnings_performance.
The text reports Tiger Global's 13F filing showing it added to its Microsoft position, which is a fund buying stock.
The headline event is Tyson lowering its 2019 earnings forecast, which is guidance and therefore earnings_performance; the 5.6% share drop is a reaction to that guidance, not the story itself.
The text concerns a lawsuit filed by Renault Spyker against General Motors, which is litigation and therefore legal_regulatory.
The text reports quarterly EPS beating estimates and revenue in line with forecasts, which is results coverage.

The headline event is the start of a late-stage clinical trial for Pfizer and BioNTech's mRNA vaccine candidate, which is R&D/product development. The partnership angle is secondary since the trial itself, not the alliance, is the story.
The text reports Amazon considering buying Toys R Us stores, which is a potential acquisition/deal story.

The text is about Nvidia unveiling a new PC processor built alongside Microsoft, which is a product launch and technology story. The Microsoft partnership is secondary context, so product_innovation is the headline event.
The text centers on a JPMorgan analyst's bullish view of large-cap consumer staples and McDonald's, which is analyst sentiment rather than a company event.
The text reports quarterly EPS beating estimates plus current-quarter and full-year guidance missing estimates, which is results and guidance coverage.
The headline event is a Jefferies downgrade to underperform, an analyst rating change, which fits market_analyst_sentiment; the premarket share move is a reaction to that rating.
The text describes Nvidia's stock price being "red hot," which is a stock price move and investor sentiment about the shares, fitting market_analyst_sentiment.

The text is a pundit's bullish/bearish commentary on Marvell's stock performance and his continued holding, which fits analyst/investor sentiment on the stock. It is not a fund or activist position disclosure, so investor_activity is only weakly defensible.

The text describes a contract between Best Buy and Brightstar Corp. for managing returned mobile device inventory, which is a strategic business development/distribution arrangement. No financial figures, deals of ownership, or product launches are involved.

The text is a macro market report on index moves driven by US retail sales data, with Intel results only mentioned as limiting Nasdaq losses; the Motorola price-target cut is a separate analyst note. The headline event is a macro data release and index move, which the rules assign to other.

The headline event is a stock price move (shares fell 2.6%) driven by reports of a Chinese ban, which fits market_analyst_sentiment as a stock price move. The underlying cause is a regulatory action by China, making legal_regulatory also defensible.

The text is a bullish investor/analyst view (Cramer) on Tessera's stock, with Apple mentioned only as a customer, so the story is analyst/investor sentiment on the stock. The mention of potential licensing deals makes partnerships a secondary but weaker fit.

The text centers on eBay's weaker-than-expected forecast and the resulting 12% stock drop, making the guidance the headline event. The share move and investor commentary are reactions to that forecast, so earnings_performance is the primary label.

The text centers on Intel's Q1 results beating expectations and strong Q2 guidance, which is earnings performance; the 15% share move is a reaction to those results, so the headline event is the earnings beat.

The Amazon item is about its Prime Now service launching one-hour delivery from local stores, a service/product expansion. It could also be read as a distribution arrangement with local stores, but the product/service is the story.

The text centers on Yahoo's pending $4.83 billion sale of its core internet business to Verizon and the possible amendment or cancellation of that deal. The executive and board departures are tied to the deal closing, making leadership_governance a secondary but defensible label.
The text is about an analyst raising a price target on Wells Fargo stock, which is squarely analyst sentiment.
The text is a pundit's bullish view on Apple's prospects from the AT&T/T-Mobile deal, which is analyst/investor sentiment about the stock rather than a deal involving Apple itself.
